summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic lymphedema, recurrent cellulitis, morbid obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, and epilepsy was admitted for worsening left leg swelling, erythema, and weeping lesions, concerning for recurrent cellulitis. She was started on IV vancomycin with pre-treatment for allergy prevention and showed clinical improvement. Her volume status was managed with IV and oral diuretics, and she reported feeling less bloated. During admission, she experienced an episode of altered mental status concerning for a possible seizure, prompting neurology consultation and follow-up planning. Warfarin was adjusted due to supratherapeutic INR, likely influenced by antibiotics. She completed a course of vancomycin and was transitioned to oral penicillin for infection prophylaxis. Discharge included home health for one final IV dose, follow-up appointments, and instructions on weight monitoring, INR checks, and medication management.
problems: Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
